mcp.note: not a runtime, local-first axis does not apply the same way - see research/protocols/mcp-2026-07-28.md

openai-agents-sdk.verdict: local-capable via explicit opt-in, not local-first by default

pydantic-ai.verdict: UNKNOWN - insufficient evidence, durable execution backends typically self-hostable

kimi-agent-sdk.verdict: UNKNOWN - genuinely unresolved after direct fetch

qwen-agent.verdict: strongest local-first signal so far - first-party vLLM/Ollama self-hosted model path

tencent-youtu-agent.verdict: CORRECTION to brief's framing: NOT confirmed local-first, cloud-configured by default

langgraph.verdict: LOCAL_CAPABLE (corrected) - the Checkpointer interface is genuinely local-native (in-memory/SQLite first-class, not a degraded fallback); Postgres/Mongo are optional production backends, not a mandatory dependency. Real caveats: langgraph-api is separately licensed (Elastic 2.0), and persistence-lifecycle (retention, schema migration) is unresolved independent of backend choice
langgraph.correction_note: first draft incorrectly framed Postgres/Redis as a production requirement implied by the SDK; corrected on user feedback with direct re-reading of the checkpointer interface

mastra.verdict: LOCAL_CAPABLE - strongest combined storage-plus-tools local-first story researched (LibSQL local file DB + Workspace filesystem/command-execution/search, both local-native with per-tool approval gating); model-execution local-first status remains UNKNOWN

installment_3_observation: local-first is not one axis; LangGraph and Mastra are each strong on checkpointing/storage-plus-tools and unresolved on model execution - per-capability columns are load-bearing, not the single verdict. LangGraph's more precise finding is persistence LIFECYCLE risk (retention, schema migration), not a local-vs-cloud backend gap.

imported_supplementary_corpus.provenance: beyond the original 17-source brief; user-supplied, not independently re-verified via WebFetch/WebSearch in this session - see individual .context/research/{name}.json files and research/imported-corpus/SOURCE-RECEIPT.md

verdicts.openhands: LOCAL_CAPABLE - local/ephemeral Agent Server workspace, Cloud also available; local mount can expose writable host files (named caveat)
verdicts.letta: LOCAL_CAPABLE - self-hostable via Docker/PostgreSQL, or managed cloud; needs Postgres, not zero-infra
verdicts.google-adk: LOCAL_CAPABLE, platform-adjacent - local/container execution exists but platform services (Agent Runtime/Cloud Run/GKE) materially expand the surface
verdicts.browser-use: LOCAL_NATIVE for the core loop - deliberately minimal thin task+environment abstraction, OSS local browser is the default
verdicts.crewai: LOCAL_CAPABLE - open-source framework and the managed AMP platform are explicitly different things

imported_supplementary_corpus_batch_2.provenance: beyond the original 17-source brief; second user-supplied 'next wave' corpus, not independently re-verified via WebFetch/WebSearch in this session - see research/comparison/NEXT-WAVE-RUNTIME-LOCAL-FIRST.md

verdicts.smolagents: LOCAL_CAPABLE - local/HF/provider model support, agent memory local by default
verdicts.llama-index: LOCAL_CAPABLE - strong local data stack, explicit disk persistence
verdicts.haystack: LOCAL_NATIVE/LOCAL_CAPABLE - HF local, llama.cpp, and Ollama all documented; strongest local-model breadth of batch 2
